page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 614 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier across most standard workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1899.98, while multi-core performance reaches 15531.7. Memory bandwidth tests show a cached read speed of 833.76 GB/sec for small blocks, dropping to 99.32 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with large block writes at 58.27 GB/sec. The system demonstrates solid capabilities in text and data processing, with a Passmark database operations score of 7947.28 and Redis SET operations reaching 15.82 million operations per second. Notably, it achieves a strong performance tier in LLM text generation for small 135M models at 265.09 tokens per second, though medium 7B models run at an average speed of 12.47 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ds_v5 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated compute, moderate memory, and fast local SSD storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides a cost-effective storage buffer for temporary files and caching. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including relational databases, web serving (with a static web serving throughput of 21.35 GB/sec), software compilation (Geekbench compiling score of 15202.0), and intermediate data processing tasks.
